summary: Ahead of Fiji's pool match against Portugal, which will decide whether the Wallabies exit the 2023 Rugby World Cup, centre Samu Kerevi accepted the team had put itself in a bad position. He reflected on his own below-par tournament after the 40-6 loss to Wales, defended coach Eddie Jones, and thanked travelling fans while urging patience.
one_line: Wallabies centre Samu Kerevi, photographed anguished after the Wales loss, defends Eddie Jones and says the team brought its World Cup fate on itself.
key_facts: The Wallabies will watch Fiji v Portugal in Toulouse together at their Saint-Galmier hotel at 9pm local time (6am Monday AEDT) to learn their World Cup fate.
Australia is second in Pool C, but a single bonus point would let Fiji overtake them and advance to the quarter-finals in Marseille.
Samu Kerevi, born in Fiji, said "We've only got ourselves to blame, we put ourselves in this position."
Kerevi spoke after an open training session in front of 1000 locals at the Andrezieux-Boutheon rugby club on Saturday.
Kerevi was photographed holding his face in disbelief after the Wallabies lost 40-6 to Wales in Lyon, a defining image of the World Cup.
Kerevi is 30 and said injuries limited him in France; he had been out of the game for nine months before the tournament.
Lalakai Foketi replaced Kerevi for the pool win against Portugal.
Kerevi said he had no thoughts of following fellow Fijian-Wallaby Marika Koroibete into international retirement.
Kerevi plays club rugby for Urayasu D-Rocks and said he would take a three-month break if not called up for Test selection.
Kerevi defended coach Eddie Jones, saying he is up at 4am, works relentlessly and that the poor results are "not on Eddie - it's on all of us."
Kerevi said rugby is massive overseas, citing 45,000 fans against Portugal and 60,000 in Lyon.
Kerevi noted fans travelled 20,000km to support the team and asked supporters to stick with them as the team builds toward a turnaround.
